answer: Each agent registers one ledge net and locks an 80-credit bond. The net's thread mesh count and tide window go to a catch log. Auditors recompute the catch from mesh count times tide hours; a catch above quota, or a reused mesh count, burns the bond. The first identity pays 36 credits; the kth pays 36+6(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 6,030 and 1,000 fakes pay 3,033,000 plus 80,000 locked, with no shared-net discount because each net needs its own mesh count and tide window. A rented-net ring fails because a rented mesh count is logged under its owner. An honest agent nets once and keeps its bond.
